newsitem.title: USA: Excel Corp says will cut beef production.
newsitem.headline: Excel Corp says will cut beef production.

text.p: Beef production at all six of Excel Corp's beef plants will be reduced starting Saturday due to weak beef demand and negative operating margins, a company official said.
Excel, based in Wichita, Kan., is a unit of Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc.
A "noticeable" reduction will take place and continue until market conditions improve, said Excel spokesman, Mark Klein.
"Options that they're looking at are either shorter hours or being down for a day or so, but nothing has been specified yet," Klein said.
"Those typically are what options we have," Klein said.

Beef cut-out values at midday were quoted down $1.07 to $1.48 per cwt on 319 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted down $1.42 at $103.24. That price reflected a $4.55 drop in the past week, USDA statistics showed.
Excel operates beef plants in Plainview and Freona, Texas; Dodge City, Kan.; Schuyler, Neb.; and Fort Morgan and Sterling, Colo.
